Let them tell how they deserved to hang formless upon Your Word in this way, unless by that same Word they were called back to Your Unity, given form, and so from You, the one supreme Good, were made all very good. How did they deserve from You even to be without form, when they would not have been even this except from You?

How did corporeal matter deserve from You even to be invisible and without form? It would not have been even this unless You had made it; and so, since it did not yet exist, it could not deserve from You to be made. Or how could the inchoate spiritual creature deserve from You even to ebb and flow in darkness like the deep, unlike You, unless it had been turned by that same Word toward the One by whom it was created, and, enlightened by Him, had become light, not equal to that Form which is equal to You, yet conformed to it? For just as in a body to be is not the same as to be beautiful (otherwise it could not be deformed), so for a created spirit to live is not the same as to live wisely (otherwise it would be wise unchangeably). But it is good for it to cling to You always, so that the light it gained by turning toward You it may not lose by turning away from You, and slip back into a life like the dark deep. For we ourselves too, who in respect of the soul are a spiritual creature, turned away from You, our light, and in that life were once darkness; and we still labor among the remnants of our darkness, until in Your Only One we become Your righteousness, like the mountains of God. For we have been Your judgments, which are like the great deep.

What You said at the first creation, Let there be light, and there was light, I understand, not unfittingly, of the spiritual creature, because there was already a life of some kind which You could illuminate. But just as it had no claim on You to be a life capable of being enlightened, so, once it existed, it had no claim on You to be enlightened. For its formless state could not have pleased You unless it became light, and became light not simply by existing, but by gazing on the Light that illuminates it and clinging to that Light. So the fact that it lives at all, and that it lives happily, it owes to nothing but Your grace, having been turned, by a change for the better, toward That which can be changed neither for the worse nor for the better. That is what You alone are, because You alone simply are; for You it is not one thing to live and another to live blessedly, since You Yourself are Your own Blessedness.

What, then, could have been lacking to Your good, which You Yourself are, even if these things had never existed at all, or had remained without form? You made them not out of any need but out of the fullness of Your goodness, restraining them and turning them toward form, and not as though Your joy were to be made complete by them. For it is to You, who are perfect, that their imperfection is displeasing, and so they are perfected by You and please You; not as though You were imperfect and were Yourself to be perfected by their perfecting. For Your good Spirit was indeed borne over the waters, not borne up by them, as if He rested upon them. For those in whom Your good Spirit is said to rest, He causes to rest in Himself. But it was Your incorruptible and unchangeable will, all-sufficient in itself for itself, that was borne over that life which You had created. For that life, to live is not the same as to live happily, since it lives even while it ebbs and flows in its own darkness; what remains for it is to be turned toward Him by whom it was made, and to live more and more by the fountain of life, and in His light to see light, and to be perfected, and enlightened, and made blessed.

See, now the Trinity appears to me in a glass darkly, the Trinity which You are, my God. For You, O Father, created heaven and earth in Him who is the Beginning of our wisdom, who is Your Wisdom, born of Yourself, equal to You and coeternal: that is, in Your Son. We have now said a great deal about the Heaven of heavens, and about the earth invisible and without form, and about the dark deep, with regard to the wandering instability of its spiritual formlessness, had it not been turned toward Him from whom it had whatever degree of life it then had, and by His enlightening become a beautiful life, and the heaven of that heaven which was afterward set between water and water. And under the name of God I now took the Father, who made these things, and under the name of Beginning, the Son, in whom He made them; and believing, as I did, that my God is the Trinity, I searched further in His holy words, and see, Your Spirit moved upon the waters. Here is the Trinity, my God: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, Creator of all creation.

But what was the reason, O Light that speaks the truth? To You I lift up my heart; do not let it teach me empty things; scatter its darkness, and tell me, I beg You, by our mother charity, tell me, I beg You, the reason why, after naming heaven, and the earth invisible and without form, and darkness upon the deep, Your Scripture only then at last names Your Spirit. Was it because it was fitting that He should be made known as being "borne above," and this could not be said unless that over which Your Spirit could be understood to be borne had been mentioned first? For He was not borne above the Father, nor above the Son, nor could He rightly be said to be borne above if He were borne above nothing. So first there had to be mention of that over which He might be borne, and then of Him, who was fittingly spoken of in no other way than as being borne above. But why was it not fitting that He should be made known in any other way than as being borne above?

From here, let whoever is able follow with his understanding Your Apostle, where he says, Because Your love is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who is given to us; and where, speaking of spiritual gifts, he teaches and shows us a more excellent way, the way of love; and where he bows his knee to You for us, that we may know the supereminent knowledge of the love of Christ. And that is why, from the beginning, He was borne supereminent above the waters. To whom shall I say this? How shall I speak of the weight of evil desires, pulling downward into the sheer abyss, and of how love lifts us up again through Your Spirit, who was borne above the waters? To whom shall I say it? How shall I say it? For it is not in places that we sink and rise again. What could be more alike, and yet what less alike? They are affections, they are loves: the uncleanness of our spirit flowing away downward with the love of cares, and the holiness of Yours lifting us upward by the love of a rest free from anxiety, so that we may lift up our hearts to You, where Your Spirit is borne above the waters, and come to that supereminent rest, when our soul has passed through the waters that are without substance.

Angels fell away, the soul of man fell away, and so they revealed the abyss in its dark depth that lay ready for the whole spiritual creation, had You not said from the beginning, Let there be light, and light had come to be, and every obedient intelligence of Your heavenly City had clung to You and rested in Your Spirit, who is borne unchangeably over everything changeable. Otherwise even the heaven of heavens would have been in itself a dark deep; but now it is light in the Lord. For even in the wretched restlessness of the spirits who fell away and laid bare their own darkness once they were stripped of the clothing of Your light, You show clearly enough how noble You made the rational creature, for which nothing less than You can suffice to give it a happy rest, and so not even itself. For You, O our God, will lighten our darkness; from You rises our garment of light, and then our darkness shall be as the noonday. Give Yourself to me, O my God, give Yourself back to me. See, I love; and if it is too little, let me love more strongly. I cannot measure it so as to know how much love I still lack before my life can run into Your embrace, and not turn away until it is hidden in the hidden place of Your Presence. This alone I know: that it goes badly with me apart from You, not only outside me but within myself as well; and all abundance that is not my God is emptiness to me.

But was neither the Father nor the Son borne above the waters? If this means in space, like a body, then neither was the Holy Spirit; but if it means the unchangeable supereminence of the Divinity above everything changeable, then Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit were all borne above the waters. Why, then, is this said only of Your Spirit? Why is it said of Him alone, as though He were in a place, He who is not in any place, and of whom alone it is written that He is Your gift? In Your Gift we rest; there we enjoy You. Our rest is our place. Love lifts us up to it, and Your good Spirit raises our lowliness from the gates of death. In Your good pleasure lies our peace. A body strives by its own weight toward its own place. Weight does not pull only downward; it pulls toward a thing's own place. Fire tends upward, a stone downward. They are moved by their own weights; they seek their own places. Oil poured under water rises above the water; water poured on top of oil sinks beneath the oil. They are moved by their own weights to seek their own places. When they are out of order they are restless; when they are restored to order they are at rest. My weight is my love; by it I am carried wherever I am carried. We are set on fire; by Your Gift we are kindled and carried upward; we glow within, and we go forward. We climb the ascents in our heart and sing a song of degrees; we glow within with Your fire, with Your good fire, and we go, because we are going upward to the peace of Jerusalem; for I was glad when they said to me, We will go up to the house of the Lord. There Your good pleasure will settle us, so that we will want nothing else than to remain there forever.

Blessed is the creature which, though it is itself other than You, has known no other condition than this: that as soon as it was made, without any interval of time, it was lifted up by Your Gift, which is borne above everything changeable, lifted up by that calling in which You said, Let there be light, and there was light. In us this happened at different times, in that we were darkness and are being made light; but of that creature it is said only what it would have been had it not been enlightened. And it is spoken of as though it had been unsettled and dark before, so that the cause by which it was made otherwise might appear: namely, that by turning to the unfailing Light it became light. Let whoever can understand this; let him ask it of You. Why should he trouble me, as if I could enlighten any man who comes into this world?

Which of us understands the Almighty Trinity? And yet which of us does not speak of It, if indeed it is It that he speaks of? Rare is the soul that knows what it is speaking of when it speaks of It. And people argue and fight, yet without peace no one sees that vision. I wish people would consider these three, which are in themselves. These three are indeed something very different from that Trinity; I am only pointing out where they may exercise themselves, and there test and feel how far off they are. The three I mean are: to be, to know, and to will. For I am, and I know, and I will: I am a knowing and willing being; I know that I am and that I will; and I will to be and to know. In these three, then, let whoever can discern how inseparable a life there is, indeed one life, one mind, and one essence; how inseparable, finally, the distinction is, and yet it is a distinction. Surely a man has this right in front of him; let him look into himself, and see, and tell me. But when he discovers something in these and can say it, let him not think on that account that he has found what is above them, the Unchangeable, which is unchangeably, and knows unchangeably, and wills unchangeably. And whether it is because of these three that there is also a Trinity in God; or whether all three are in Each, so that the three belong to Each; or whether both are true at once, in wondrous ways, simply and yet manifoldly, Itself a bound to Itself within Itself and yet unbounded, by which It is, and is known to Itself, and suffices to Itself, unchangeably the Selfsame, by the abundant greatness of Its Unity: who can easily conceive of this? Who could express it in any way? Who would in any way pronounce on it rashly?

Go on with your confession, O my faith; say to the Lord your God, Holy, Holy, Holy, O Lord my God, in Your Name we have been baptized, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; in Your Name we baptize, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. For among us too, in His Christ, God made heaven and earth: that is, the spiritual and the carnal people of His Church. And our earth, before it received the form of doctrine, was invisible and without form, and we were covered with the darkness of ignorance. For You chastened man for iniquity, and Your judgments were like the great deep to him. But because Your Spirit was borne above the waters, Your mercy did not abandon our misery, and You said, Let there be light: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. Repent; let there be light. And because our soul was troubled within us, we remembered You, O Lord, from the land of Jordan, and from that mountain equal to You, but little for our sake; and our darkness displeased us, and we turned to You, and there was light. And see, we were once darkness, but now we are light in the Lord.

And yet it is still by faith and not yet by sight, for we are saved by hope; but hope that is seen is not hope. Still deep calls to deep, but now in the voice of Your waterspouts. Still, even he who says, I could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal, even he does not yet consider himself to have laid hold of it; he forgets what lies behind and reaches forward to what lies ahead, and groans under his burden, and his soul thirsts for the Living God, as the deer for the water brooks, and says, When shall I come? longing to be clothed over with his dwelling which is from heaven. And he calls to this lower deep, saying, Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind; and, Do not be children in understanding, but in malice be children, so that in understanding you may be perfect; and, O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you? But now he speaks no longer in his own voice, but in Yours, who sent Your Spirit from above through Him who ascended on high and opened the floodgates of His gifts, so that the force of His streams might make glad the city of God. It is for Him that this friend of the Bridegroom sighs, already having the first fruits of the Spirit laid up with Him, yet still groaning within himself, waiting for the adoption, that is, the redemption of his body. For Him he sighs, since he is a member of the Bride; for Him he is jealous, since he is a friend of the Bridegroom; for Him he is jealous, not for himself. For it is in the voice of Your waterspouts, not in his own voice, that he calls to that other deep, over which, in his jealousy, he is afraid that, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, so their minds may be corrupted from the purity that is in our Bridegroom, Your only Son. O what a light of beauty that will be, when we shall see Him as He is, and those tears have passed away which have been my bread day and night, while they say to me every day, Where is your God now?

See, I too say, O my God, where are You? See, there You are! In You I breathe a little, when I pour out my soul within me in the voice of joy and praise, the sound of one keeping festival. And yet it is sad again, because it slips back and becomes a deep, or rather feels that it is still a deep. My faith, which You have kindled to light my feet in the night, speaks to it: Why are you sad, O my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in the Lord; His word is a lamp to your feet. Hope and endure, until the night, the mother of the wicked, has passed, until the wrath of the Lord has passed, whose children we too once were, we who were once darkness, whose remnants we still carry about in our body, dead because of sin; until the day breaks and the shadows flee away. Hope in the Lord: in the morning I shall stand in Your presence and contemplate You; I shall confess to You forever. In the morning I shall stand in Your presence and see the health of my countenance, my God, who will also give life to our mortal bodies by the Spirit who dwells in us, because in His mercy He was borne over our dark and fluid inner deep. From Him, in this pilgrimage, we have received a pledge that we should already be light, while we are still saved by hope, and are children of light and children of the day, not children of the night nor of the darkness, which nevertheless we once were. Between those children of darkness and us, in this still uncertain state of human knowledge, You alone draw the dividing line: You who test our hearts, and call the light day and the darkness night. For who distinguishes us but You? And what do we have that we did not receive from You? Out of the same lump vessels are made for honor, from which others too are made for dishonor.

Or who but You, our God, made for us that firmament of authority over us in Your Divine Scripture? As it is said, For heaven shall be folded up like a scroll; and now it is stretched over us like a skin. For Your Divine Scripture carries a loftier authority now that those mortals through whom You dispensed it to us have undergone that mortality. And You know, Lord, You know, how You clothed men with skins when through sin they became mortal. So You have stretched out the firmament of Your book like a skin, that is, Your harmonious words, which through the ministry of mortal men You have spread over us. For by their very death that solid firmament of authority, in Your words set forth by them, was stretched out on high over everything beneath it, though while they lived here it had not been stretched out so high. You had not yet spread out the heaven like a skin; You had not yet spread abroad on every side the renown of their deaths.

Let us look, O Lord, upon the heavens, the work of Your fingers; clear from our eyes the cloud You have spread beneath them. There is Your testimony, which gives wisdom to the little ones. Perfect, O my God, Your praise out of the mouths of babes and sucklings. For we know no other books that so destroy pride, that so destroy the enemy and the defender, who resists Your reconciliation by defending his own sins. I do not know, Lord, I do not know any other words so pure, which so persuade me to confess, and make my neck bend to Your yoke, and invite me to serve You for nothing in return. Let me understand them, good Father; grant me this, since I am placed beneath them, because it is for those placed beneath them that You have established them.

There are other waters above this firmament, immortal, I believe, and set apart from earthly corruption. Let them praise Your Name, let them praise You, those supercelestial peoples, Your angels, who have no need to gaze up at this firmament or to come to know Your Word by reading. For they always behold Your face, and there, without any syllables of time, they read what Your eternal will wills. They read, they choose, they love. They are always reading, and what they read never passes away; for by choosing and by loving they read the very unchangeableness of Your counsel. Their book is never closed, and their scroll is never folded up, because You Yourself are this to them, and are so eternally; for You have ordained them above this firmament, which You have made firm over the weakness of the lower peoples, so that they might gaze up at it and come to know Your mercy, which proclaims in time You who made times. For Your mercy, O Lord, is in the heavens, and Your truth reaches to the clouds. The clouds pass away, but the heaven remains. The preachers of Your word pass out of this life into another; but Your Scripture is spread out over the peoples, even to the end of the world. Yet heaven and earth too shall pass away, but Your words shall not pass away. For the scroll shall be rolled up, and the grass over which it was spread shall pass away with all its beauty; but Your Word remains forever. Now it appears to us in the dark image of the clouds and through the mirror of the heavens, not as it is; because even we, though we are the well-beloved of Your Son, it has not yet appeared what we shall be. He looked through the lattice of our flesh, and spoke tenderly to us, and set us on fire, and we run after His fragrance. But when He appears, then we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is. As He is, Lord: that will be our seeing, though it is not yet ours.

For only You know fully what You are: You who are unchangeably, and know unchangeably, and will unchangeably. Your Essence knows and wills unchangeably; Your Knowledge is and wills unchangeably; and Your Will is and knows unchangeably. Nor does it seem right in Your eyes that the Unchangeable Light should be known by what is enlightened and changeable in the way It knows Itself. That is why my soul is like a land where there is no water: for just as it cannot enlighten itself from itself, so it cannot satisfy itself from itself. For just so is the fountain of life with You, as in Your light we shall see light.

Who gathered the embittered together into one society? For they all have one and the same end, a temporal and earthly happiness, for the sake of which they do everything, though they toss up and down amid a countless variety of cares. Who, Lord, but You, who said, Let the waters be gathered together into one place, and let the dry land appear, the land that thirsts for You? For the sea too is Yours, and You made it, and Your hands formed the dry land. For it is not the bitterness of men's wills but the gathering together of the waters that is called sea. For You also restrain the wicked desires of men's souls and fix their bounds, how far they may be allowed to go, so that their waves may break against one another; and so You make it a sea, by the order of Your dominion over all things.

But the souls that thirst for You and appear before You, set apart from the society of the sea by a different end, You water from a hidden and sweet spring, so that the earth may bring forth its fruit; and at Your command, O Lord God, our soul buds forth works of mercy according to their kind, loving our neighbor by relieving his bodily needs, having seed in itself according to its likeness, when from a sense of our own weakness we feel compassion so as to help the needy, aiding them as we would want to be aided if we were in the same need. And this not only in easy things, like the herb yielding seed, but also in the protection of our help, with all our strength, like the tree yielding fruit: that is, by doing good in rescuing the one who suffers wrong from the hand of the powerful, and giving him the shelter of protection through the mighty strength of just judgment.

So, Lord, so, I beg You, let it spring up, as You make it do, as You give cheerfulness and ability: let truth spring out of the earth, and righteousness look down from heaven, and let there be lights in the firmament. Let us break our bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into our house. Let us clothe the naked, and not despise those of our own flesh. When these fruits have sprung from the earth, see that it is good; and let our light break forth in its season. And let us, rising from this lower fruitfulness of action to the delight of contemplation, and holding fast the Word of Life above, appear like lights in the world, clinging to the firmament of Your Scripture. For there You teach us to divide between things intellectual and things of sense, as between day and night, or between souls given to things intellectual and souls given to things of sense. So now it is not You alone, in the secret of Your judgment, who divide between the light and the darkness, as before the firmament was made; but Your spiritual children too, set and ranked in that same firmament, now that Your grace has been laid open throughout the world, may give light upon the earth, and divide between day and night, and be for signs of the times: signs that old things have passed away, and, behold, all things have become new; that our salvation is nearer than when we believed; that the night is far spent and the day is at hand; and that You will crown Your year with blessing, sending the laborers of Your goodness into Your harvest, which others labored to sow, and sending them also into another field, whose harvest will come at the end. So You grant the prayers of the one who asks, and bless the years of the just; but You are the same, and in Your years, which do not fail, You prepare a granary for our passing years. For by an eternal counsel You bestow heavenly blessings on the earth in their proper seasons. For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom, as it were the greater light, for the sake of those who delight in the light of clear truth, as for the rule of the day. To another is given the word of knowledge by the same Spirit, as it were the lesser light; to another faith; to another the gift of healing; to another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another the discerning of spirits; to another different kinds of tongues. And all these are like stars. For all these are the work of one and the same Spirit, dividing to each person his own as He wills, and making stars appear in plain view, for the common good. But the word of knowledge, in which all the Sacraments are contained, which vary with their seasons like the moon, and those other notices of gifts which are listed after it, like stars, fall short of that brightness of wisdom in which the day just mentioned rejoices, and so they belong only to the rule of the night. For they are necessary to those whom Your most prudent servant could not speak to as spiritual but only as carnal, he who speaks wisdom among those who are perfect. But the natural man, like a babe in Christ who is fed on milk, until he is strong enough for solid food and his eye is made able to look at the Sun, should not be left in a night abandoned by all light, but should be content with the light of the moon and the stars. So You speak with us, our all-wise God, in Your Book, Your firmament, so that we may discern all things in wonderful contemplation, though still in signs and in seasons, and in days and in years.

But first, wash yourselves, be clean; put away evil from your souls and from before My eyes, so that the dry land may appear. Learn to do good, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow, so that the earth may bring forth the green herb for food, and the tree bearing fruit; and come, let us reason together, says the Lord, so that there may be lights in the firmament of heaven, and they may shine upon the earth. That rich man asked the good Master what he should do to gain eternal life. Let the good Master tell him (the rich man thought Him no more than a man, but He is good because He is God), let Him tell him that if he wants to enter into life he must keep the commandments: let him put away from himself the bitterness of malice and wickedness; let him not kill, not commit adultery, not steal, not bear false witness; so that the dry land may appear and bring forth honor for father and mother and love for our neighbor. All these, he says, I have kept. Then where do so many thorns come from, if the earth is fruitful? Go, root out the spreading thickets of covetousness; sell what you have, and be filled with fruit by giving to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and follow the Lord if you want to be perfect, joined with those among whom He speaks wisdom, He who knows what to assign to the day and what to the night, so that you too may know it, and so that for you too there may be lights in the firmament of heaven. That will not happen unless your heart is there; and that in turn will not happen unless your treasure is there, as you have heard from the good Master. But that barren earth was grieved, and the thorns choked the word.

But you, chosen generation, you weak things of the world, who have left everything to follow the Lord: go after Him, and put the mighty to shame; go after Him, you beautiful feet, and shine in the firmament, so that the heavens may declare His glory, dividing between the light of the perfect, though they are not yet as the angels, and the darkness of the little ones, though they are not despaired of. Shine over all the earth; and let the day, bright with the sun, utter to day the speech of wisdom, and let the night, shining with the moon, show to night the word of knowledge. The moon and the stars shine for the night, yet the night does not darken them, since they give it light in its measure. For see, it is as if God were saying, Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven: suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a rushing mighty wind, and there appeared divided tongues as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And lights were made in the firmament of heaven, holding the word of life. Run everywhere, you holy fires, you beautiful fires; for you are the light of the world, and you are not put under a bushel. He to whom you cling is exalted, and He has exalted you. Run everywhere, and make yourselves known to all nations.

May the sea, too, conceive your works and give birth to them, and may the waters bring forth the moving creature that has life. For in setting apart what is precious from what is worthless you have become God's mouth, and through you He says, Let the waters bring forth: not the living creature that the earth produces, but the moving creature that has life, and the birds that fly above the earth. For Your Sacraments, O God, have made their way through the work of Your holy ones, moving in the midst of the world's waves of temptation, to steep the Gentiles in Your Name, in Your Baptism. And meanwhile great and wonderful works were done, like great whales; and the voices of Your messengers went flying above the earth, along the open firmament of Your Book, which stood over them as the authority beneath which they were to fly, wherever they might go. For there is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard, since their sound has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world, because You, Lord, multiplied these things by Your blessing.

Am I speaking falsely, or am I mixing and confusing things, and failing to distinguish between the clear knowledge of these things in the firmament of heaven and the material works in the billowing sea and under the firmament of heaven? For there are things whose knowledge is solid and defined, without any increase by generation, like lights of wisdom and knowledge; yet of those very things the material operations are many and various, and as one thing grows out of another they are multiplied by Your blessing, O God, who have refreshed the jaded senses of mortals, so that one thing grasped in the understanding of our mind may be set forth and expressed in many ways through the motions of the body. These Sacraments the waters have brought forth, but in Your word. The needs of peoples estranged from the eternity of Your truth have brought them forth, but in Your Gospel; because the waters themselves cast them forth, and it was their diseased bitterness that caused these things to be sent forth in Your Word.

All the things You have made are beautiful; but look, You who made them all are more beautiful beyond all telling. If Adam had not fallen away from You, the salt brine of the sea would never have poured out of him — that is, the human race, so deeply curious, so stormily swelling, so restlessly tossing to and fro. And then there would have been no need for Your stewards to work mysterious deeds and utter mysterious words in many waters, in a bodily and sensible way. For this is what those moving and flying creatures now seem to me to mean: that people instructed and initiated through bodily Sacraments would make no further progress unless their soul came alive with a spiritual life, and unless, after the word of admission, it looked ahead toward perfection.

And so, in Your Word, it is not the depth of the sea but the earth, separated from the bitterness of the waters, that brings forth — not the moving creature that has life, but the living soul. For now it no longer needs baptism, as the heathen need it, and as it needed it itself when it was covered with the waters (for there is no other way into the kingdom of heaven, since You have appointed that this should be the way in). Nor does it look for wondrous miracles to produce belief; for it is not the kind that will not believe unless it sees signs and wonders, now that the faithful earth has been separated from the waters that were bitter with unbelief, and tongues are a sign not for those who believe but for those who do not believe. So that earth which You founded upon the waters has no need of the flying kind either, which the waters brought forth at Your word. Send Your word into it through Your messengers: for we tell of their works, yet it is You who work in them, so that they may work out a living soul in it. The earth brings it forth, because the earth is the cause of their doing this in the soul, just as the sea was the cause of their working upon the moving creatures that have life and the birds that fly under the firmament of heaven. The earth has no need of these now, although it feeds on that Fish which was lifted out of the deep, at that table which You have prepared in the presence of those who believe. For this is why He was lifted out of the deep: to feed the dry land. And the birds, though bred in the sea, still multiply upon the earth. For human unbelief was the cause of the first preaching of the Evangelists; yet the faithful too are exhorted and blessed by them in many ways, day after day. But the living soul takes its beginning from the earth: for it profits only those already among the Faithful to hold themselves back from love of this world, so that their soul may live to You — the soul that was dead while it lived in pleasures, in pleasures that bring death, Lord; for You, Lord, are the life-giving delight of the pure heart.

So now let Your ministers work upon the earth — not as they did upon the waters of unbelief, by preaching and speaking through miracles and Sacraments and mystic words, where ignorance, the mother of wonder, might be held fixed on them out of awe toward those hidden signs. For that is the way into the Faith for the sons of Adam who have forgotten You, while they hide themselves from Your face and become a dark deep. But let Your ministers work now as on the dry land, separated from the whirlpools of the great deep; and let them be a pattern to the Faithful by living before them and stirring them to imitation. For in this way people hear not only in order to hear, but in order to do as well. Seek the Lord, and your soul shall live, so that the earth may bring forth the living soul. Do not be conformed to the world. Hold yourselves back from it: the soul lives by shunning what it dies by craving. Hold yourselves back from the savage wildness of pride, the sluggish sensuality of luxury, and the false name of knowledge, so that the wild beasts may be tamed, the cattle broken to the yoke, and the serpents made harmless. For in allegory these are the motions of our mind: that is, the haughtiness of pride, the delight of lust and the poison of curiosity are the motions of a dead soul. For the soul does not die in such a way as to lose all motion; it dies by forsaking the fountain of life, and so it is taken up by this passing world and conformed to it.

But Your word, O God, is the fountain of eternal life, and it does not pass away. That is why this departure of the soul is held in check by Your word, when it is said to us, Do not be conformed to this world, so that the earth, in the fountain of life, may bring forth a living soul: that is, a soul made continent in Your Word by Your Evangelists, through following those who follow Your Christ. For this is after its kind, because a man tends to imitate his friend. Be as I am (he says), for I also am as you are. So in this living soul there will be good beasts, in gentleness of action (for You have commanded, Go on with your business in meekness, and you will be loved by all men); and good cattle, which neither have too much if they eat nor go in want if they do not eat; and good serpents, not dangerous so as to do harm, but wise so as to take care, and searching into this temporal nature only as far as is enough for eternity to be clearly seen, being understood through the things that are made. For these creatures obey reason when, held back from their deadly advance upon us, they live, and are good.

For look, O Lord our God, our Creator: when our affections have been held back from love of the world, by which we were dying through living badly, and have begun to be a living soul through living well; and when Your word, which You spoke through Your apostle, has been fulfilled in us, Do not be conformed to this world; then there follows also what You added at once, saying, But be transformed by the renewing of your mind. This is no longer after your kind, as though you were following the neighbor who went ahead of you, or living by the example of some better man (for You did not say, "Let man be made after his kind," but, Let us make man after our own image and likeness), so that we may prove what Your will is. For this was the aim of that steward of Yours, who fathered children through the Gospel: he did not want to keep them babies forever, to be fed with milk and nursed as by a nurse, and so he says, Be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God. That is why You do not say, "Let man be made," but Let us make man. Nor did You say, "according to his kind," but, after our image and likeness. For a man renewed in his mind, who sees and understands Your truth, does not need another man to direct him so that he follows his own kind; with You directing him, he himself proves what is that good, that acceptable and perfect will of Yours. Indeed, You teach him, now that he is capable of it, to see the Trinity of the Unity and the Unity of the Trinity. That is why, after the plural Let us make man, the singular follows, And God made man; and after the plural After our likeness, the singular follows, After the image of God. So man is renewed in the knowledge of God, after the image of Him who created him; and once he has been made spiritual, he judges all things (all things, that is, which are to be judged), yet he himself is judged by no one.

But his judging all things corresponds to his having dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the air, and over all cattle and wild beasts, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth. For he does this by the understanding of his mind, through which he perceives the things of the Spirit of God; whereas otherwise man, set in honor, had no understanding, and is compared to the brute beasts, and has become like them. In Your Church, therefore, O our God, according to Your grace which You have bestowed on it (for we are Your workmanship, created for good works), not only those who are spiritually set over others, but also those who are spiritually subject to those set over them — for in this way You made man male and female in Your spiritual grace, where, according to the sex of the body, there is neither male nor female, because there is neither Jew nor Greek, neither slave nor free — spiritual people, then, whether those who are set over others or those who obey, judge spiritually. They do not judge of that spiritual knowledge which shines in the firmament (for it is not right to pass judgment on so supreme an authority); nor may they judge of Your Book itself, even if something in it does not shine clearly; for we submit our understanding to it, and hold as certain that even what is closed to our sight is rightly and truly spoken. For in this way man, though now spiritual and renewed in the knowledge of God after the image of Him who created him, ought to be a doer of the law, not its judge. Nor does he judge of that distinction between spiritual and carnal people, who are known to Your eyes, O our God, and have not yet shown themselves to us by their works, so that by their fruits we might know them; but You, Lord, already know them, and have divided and called them in secret, before ever the firmament was made. Nor does the spiritual man judge the restless peoples of this world; for what business has he judging those who are outside, when he does not know which of them will one day come into the sweetness of Your grace, and which will remain in the everlasting bitterness of ungodliness?

Man, then, whom You have made after Your own image, did not receive dominion over the lights of heaven, nor over that hidden heaven itself, nor over the day and the night, which You called before the foundation of the heaven, nor over the gathering together of the waters, which is the sea; but he received dominion over the fish of the sea, and the birds of the air, and over all cattle, and over all the earth, and over all creeping things that creep upon the earth. For he judges and approves what he finds right, and rejects what he finds wrong, whether in the celebration of those Sacraments by which those whom Your mercy searches out in many waters are initiated; or in the one in which that Fish is set forth which, lifted out of the deep, the devout earth feeds upon; or in the expressions and signs of words, subject to the authority of Your Book — signs that come out of the mouth and sound forth, flying as it were under the firmament, in interpreting, expounding, discoursing, disputing, blessing, or praying to You, so that the people may answer, Amen. The reason all these words have to be pronounced aloud is the deep of this world and the blindness of the flesh, which cannot see thoughts, so that it is necessary to speak loudly into the ears. So, although the flying birds multiply upon the earth, they still take their origin from the waters. The spiritual man also judges, approving what is right and rejecting what he finds wrong, in the works and lives of the faithful: their almsgiving, which is like the earth bearing fruit; and the living soul, which lives by the taming of its affections, in chastity, in fasting, in holy meditations on those things which are perceived by the senses of the body. For it is these things that he is now said to judge, the things over which he also has the power of correction.

But what is this, and what sort of mystery is it? Look, You bless mankind, O Lord, so that they may increase and multiply and fill the earth; are You not giving us a hint by this, so that we may understand something? Why did You not bless in the same way the light, which You called day, or the firmament of heaven, or the lights, or the stars, or the earth, or the sea? I might say, O God, You who created us after Your Image, I might say that it had been Your good pleasure to bestow this blessing on man alone, if You had not blessed the fishes and the whales in the same way, that they should increase and multiply and fill the waters of the sea, and that the birds should multiply upon the earth. I might likewise say that this blessing belonged properly to those creatures that reproduce from their own kind, if I had found it given to the fruit trees and plants and the beasts of the earth. But as it is, Increase and multiply is not said to the herbs or the trees, or to the beasts or the serpents, even though all these, as well as fishes, birds and men, increase by generation and preserve their kind.

What then shall I say, O Truth, my Light? "That it was said idly, and with no meaning?" Not at all, O Father of piety; far be it from a minister of Your word to say that. And if I do not understand what You mean by that phrase, let my betters — that is, those with more understanding than I have — make better use of it, according as You, my God, have given each one to understand. But let my confession also be pleasing in Your sight, in which I confess to You that I believe, O Lord, that You did not speak like this in vain; nor will I keep silent about what this reading suggests to me. For it is true, and I do not see what should prevent me from understanding the figurative sayings of Your Bible in this way. For I know that a thing understood in one way by the mind may be signified in many ways by bodily expressions, and that a thing signified in one way by bodily expression may be understood in many ways by the mind. Look at the single love of God and of our neighbor: by how many sacraments, in how countless languages, and in each language in how countless ways of speaking, it is expressed in bodily form! This is how the offspring of the waters increase and multiply. Notice again, whoever you are who read this: look, what Scripture presents and the voice pronounces in only one way, In the Beginning God created heaven and earth — is it not understood in many ways, not through any deceit of error, but through various kinds of true understanding? This is how the offspring of men increase and multiply.

If, then, we think about the natures of the things themselves, not allegorically but literally, the phrase increase and multiply applies to all things that come from seed. But if we treat these words as spoken figuratively (which I rather think is what Scripture intended, since it surely does not assign this blessing only to the offspring of water creatures and of man for no reason), then we do find "multitude" among creatures spiritual and bodily, as in heaven and earth; among the righteous and the unrighteous, as in light and darkness; among the holy authors through whom the Law was ministered to us, as in the firmament set firm between the waters and the waters; in the society of peoples still in the bitterness of unbelief, as in the sea; in the zeal of holy souls, as in the dry land; in works of mercy belonging to this present life, as in the herbs bearing seed and the trees bearing fruit; in spiritual gifts displayed for edification, as in the lights of heaven; and in affections formed to temperance, as in the living soul. In all these we meet with multitudes, abundance and increase. But something that increases and multiplies in such a way that one thing is expressed in many ways, and one expression is understood in many ways, we find only in signs expressed in bodily form and in things conceived by the mind. By signs uttered in bodily form we understand the generations of the waters, which are made necessary by the depth of the flesh; by things conceived by the mind, human generations, because of the fruitfulness of reason. And this is why we believe that You, Lord, said to both these kinds, Increase and multiply. For in this blessing I take it that You have granted us the faculty and power both to express in many ways what we understand in only one, and to understand in many ways what we read as set down obscurely in only one. This is how the waters of the sea are filled, which are not moved except by various meanings; and this is how the earth too is filled with human offspring — the earth whose dryness shows itself in its longing, and over which reason rules.

I would also like to say, O Lord my God, what the next part of Your Scripture reminds me of; indeed, I will say it, and I will not be afraid. For I will say what is true, as You inspire me with what You wanted me to draw from those words. For I do not believe that I speak truth by any inspiration other than Yours, since You are the Truth, and every man a liar. So he who speaks a lie speaks of his own; and therefore, so that I may speak truth, I will speak of what is Yours. Look, You have given us for food every herb bearing seed which is upon all the earth, and every tree in which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed. And not to us alone, but also to all the birds of the air, and to the beasts of the earth, and to all creeping things; but to the fishes and the great whales You have not given them. Now we said that these fruits of the earth signify, and figure in allegory, the works of mercy which are provided out of the fruitful earth for the needs of this life. Such an earth was the devout Onesiphorus, to whose house You gave mercy, because he often refreshed Your Paul and was not ashamed of his chain. The brethren did this too, and bore such fruit, when they supplied from Macedonia what he lacked. But how he grieves over certain trees that did not give him the fruit owed to him, when he says, At my first defense no one stood by me, but all forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge. For these fruits are owed to those who minister spiritual doctrine to us out of their understanding of the divine mysteries; and they are owed to them as men; and owed to them also as the living soul, since they offer themselves as an example in all continence; and owed to them also as flying creatures, because of their blessings which are multiplied upon the earth, since their sound has gone out into all lands.

But the ones who are fed by these fruits are those who delight in them; and those whose god is their belly do not delight in them. For even in those who give them, the fruit is not the things they give, but the spirit in which they give them. So I see clearly why he rejoiced, the man who served God and not his own belly; I see it, and I rejoice with him. For he had received from the Philippians what they had sent him by Epaphroditus; and yet I see why he rejoiced. For what he rejoiced at is what he fed on; for, speaking in truth, he says, I rejoiced greatly in the Lord, that now at last your care for me has flourished again; you were indeed caring, but it had become wearisome to you. These Philippians, then, had dried up through long weariness and withered, as it were, in bearing this fruit of a good work; and he rejoices for them, because they flourished again, not for himself, because they relieved his wants. That is why he goes on, Not that I speak in respect of want, for I have learned to be content in whatever state I am. I know both how to be brought low and how to abound; everywhere and in all things I have been taught both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Him who strengthens me.

What then do you rejoice at, great Paul? What do you rejoice at? What do you feed on, O man renewed in the knowledge of God after the image of Him who created you, you living soul of such great continence, you tongue like the flying birds, speaking mysteries? (For it is to such creatures that this food is owed.) What is it that feeds you? Joy. Let us hear what follows: Nevertheless, you have done well in sharing my affliction. This is what he rejoices at, this is what he feeds on: that they had done well, not that his hardship had been eased — he who says to You, You have enlarged me when I was in distress; for he knew how both to abound and to suffer want in You, who strengthen him. For you Philippians also know (he says) that in the beginning of the Gospel, when I left Macedonia, no Church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving but you only. For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again for my need. He now rejoices that they have returned to these good works, and is glad that they have flourished again, as when a fruitful field grows green once more.

Was it for his own needs, since he said, You sent for my need? Is that why he rejoices? Certainly not. But how do we know this? Because he himself says immediately afterward, Not because I desire a gift, but I desire fruit. I have learned from You, my God, to distinguish between a gift and fruit. A gift is the thing itself that is given by the one who shares these necessities with us, such as money, food, drink, clothing, shelter, help. But the fruit is the good and right will of the giver. For the Good Master did not say only, He who receives a prophet, but added, in the name of a prophet; nor did He say only, He who receives a righteous man, but added, in the name of a righteous man. So indeed the one will receive a prophet's reward, and the other a righteous man's reward. Nor does He say only, He who gives one of my little ones a cup of cold water to drink, but added, in the name of a disciple; and so He concludes, Truly I say to you, he shall not lose his reward. The gift is to receive a prophet, to receive a righteous man, to give a cup of cold water to a disciple; but the fruit is to do this in the name of a prophet, in the name of a righteous man, in the name of a disciple. Elijah was fed with fruit by the widow who knew that she was feeding a man of God, and fed him for that very reason; but by the raven he was fed with a gift. And it was not the inner Elijah who was fed in that way, but only the outer, who might also have perished for lack of that food.

So I will say what is true in Your sight, O Lord. When carnal people and unbelievers (for whose winning and initiation the initiatory Sacraments and the mighty works of miracles are necessary, which we take to be signified by the name of fishes and whales) undertake to refresh Your servants bodily, or to help them in some other way with something useful for this present life, then, since they do not know why this ought to be done or what end it serves, neither do they feed these servants, nor are the servants fed by them; for the givers do not act from a holy and right intention, and the others do not rejoice at their gifts, in which they do not yet see any fruit. For the mind is fed on whatever makes it glad. And that is why the fishes and whales do not feed on such food as the earth brings forth only after it has been separated and divided from the bitterness of the sea's waves.

And You, O God, saw everything that You had made, and, behold, it was very good. Yes, we too see the same, and look, all things are very good. In each separate kind of Your works, when You had said "let them be," and they were, You saw of each that it was good. Seven times I have counted it written that You saw that what You made was good; and this is the eighth, that You saw everything that You had made, and, behold, it was not only good but also very good, as being now all together. For taken one by one they were only good; but all together they were both good and very good. All beautiful bodies declare the same thing; for a body made up of members that are all beautiful is far more beautiful than those same members are on their own, by whose well-ordered blending the whole is completed, even though the members are also beautiful one by one.

And I looked closely to find whether You saw seven or eight times that Your works were good, when they pleased You; but in Your seeing I found no times by which I might understand that You saw what You made so many times. And I said, "Lord, is not this Scripture of Yours true, since You are true and, being Truth, have set it forth? Why then do You tell me 'that in Your seeing there are no times,' while this Scripture of Yours tells me that what You made each day, You saw that it was good; and when I counted them, I found how many times?" To this You answer me, for You are my God, and with a strong voice You speak to Your servant in his inner ear, breaking through my deafness and crying out, "O man, what My Scripture says, I say; and yet it speaks in time, whereas time has no bearing on My Word, because My Word exists in equal eternity with Myself. So the things you see through My Spirit, I see, just as what you speak through My Spirit, I speak. And so, while you see those things in time, I do not see them in time; just as, while you speak in time, I do not speak them in time."

And I heard, O Lord my God, and drank up a drop of sweetness from Your truth, and I understood that there are certain people who dislike Your works, and who say that You made many of them under compulsion of necessity, such as the fabric of the heavens and the harmony of the stars; and that You did not make them from what was Yours, but that they had already been created elsewhere and from other sources, for You to bring together and fit and join into one, when You built up the walls of the universe out of Your conquered enemies, so that, bound down by that structure, they could not rebel against You again. Other things, they say, You neither made nor even put together, such as all flesh and all the tiniest creatures, and whatever holds to the earth by its roots; but a mind hostile to You, and another nature not created by You and contrary to You, begot and shaped these things in the lower regions of the world. Those who say this are out of their minds, because they do not see Your works through Your Spirit, nor recognize You in them.

But those who see these things through Your Spirit — it is You who see in them. So when they see that these things are good, You see that they are good; and whatever things please for Your sake, it is You who please in them; and the things that please us through Your Spirit please You in us. For what man knows the things of a man, except the spirit of man which is in him? Even so no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God. Now we (he says) have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we might know the things that are freely given to us by God. And I am prompted to say, "Surely no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God: how then do we too know the things that are given us by God?" The answer comes to me: "Because the things we know by His Spirit, even these no one knows except the Spirit of God. For just as it was rightly said to those who were to speak by the Spirit of God, it is not you who speak, so it is rightly said to those who know through the Spirit of God, 'It is not you who know.' And no less rightly, then, is it said to those who see through the Spirit of God, 'It is not you who see'; so whatever they see through the Spirit of God to be good, it is not they but God who sees that it is good." It is one thing, then, for someone to think that what is good is evil, as those just mentioned do; another for a person to see that what is good is good (as Your creatures please many people because they are good, and yet You do not please them in those creatures, since they would rather enjoy the creatures than You); and another again for God, when a person sees that something is good, to see in him that it is good — so, that is, that He may be loved in what He made, He who cannot be loved except through the Holy Spirit whom He has given. For the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who is given to us: through whom we see that whatever exists in any degree is good. For it comes from Him who does not exist merely in some degree, but what He Is, Is.

Thanks be to You, O Lord. We see heaven and earth, whether the bodily part, higher and lower, or the spiritual and the bodily creation; and in the adorning of these parts, of which the whole mass of the world, or rather the whole of creation, consists, we see light made and divided from the darkness. We see the firmament of heaven, whether that primary body of the world between the spiritual upper waters and the lower bodily waters, or (since this too is called heaven) this space of air through which the birds of heaven wander, between those waters which are carried above it as vapor and on clear nights fall as dew, and those heavier waters which flow along the earth. We see the face of the waters gathered together in the fields of the sea; and the dry land, both bare and then formed so as to be visible and ordered, and the matter of herbs and trees as well. We see the lights shining from above, the sun to suffice for the day, the moon and the stars to comfort the night, and all these marking and signifying times. We see on every side a moist element, made fruitful with fishes, beasts and birds, because the density of the air, which bears up the flight of birds, thickens through the exhalation of the waters. We see the face of the earth adorned with earthly creatures, and man, created after Your image and likeness, set over all irrational creatures by that very image and likeness of Yours, that is, by the power of reason and understanding. And just as in his soul there is one power which rules by directing and another made subject so that it may obey, so for the man a woman was made, in bodily form as well, who in her mind, with its rational understanding, would have an equal nature, but in the sex of her body would be subject to the male sex in the same way as the drive to act is made subject so as to conceive, from the reason of the mind, the skill of acting rightly. These things we see, and each of them is good, and all together they are very good.

Your works praise You, so that we may love You; and we love You, so that Your works may praise You. They have from time a beginning and an end, a rising and a setting, growth and decay, form and privation. So they have their succession of morning and evening, partly hidden, partly plain; for they were made from nothing by You, not from You; not from any matter that was not Yours or that existed beforehand, but from concreated matter, that is, matter created by You at the same time, because You gave form to its formlessness without any interval of time. For since the matter of heaven and earth is one thing and their form another, You made the matter from absolutely nothing, but the form of the world out of the formless matter; yet You made both together, so that the form followed the matter with no pause of delay between them.

We have also looked into what You wished to be foreshadowed, whether by the creation of things in such an order or by the account of them in such an order. And we have seen that things one by one are good, and together very good, in Your Word, in Your Only-Begotten — both heaven and earth, the Head and the body of the Church — in Your predestination before all times, without morning and evening. But when You began to carry out in time what You had predestined, so that You might reveal hidden things and set our disorder in order (for our sins hung over us, and we had sunk into the dark deep, and Your good Spirit was borne over us to help us in due season), You justified the ungodly and divided them from the wicked; and You made the firmament of the authority of Your Book between those placed above, who were to be teachable toward You, and those below, who were to be subject to them. And You gathered the society of unbelievers together into one conspiracy, so that the zeal of the faithful might appear, and they might bring forth works of mercy, even distributing their earthly riches to the poor in order to gain heavenly ones. After this You kindled certain lights in the firmament, Your Holy ones, who have the word of life and shine with an eminent authority raised on high through spiritual gifts. After that again, to initiate the unbelieving Gentiles, You produced out of bodily matter the Sacraments and visible miracles and forms of words according to the firmament of Your Book, by which the faithful too should be blessed and multiplied. Next You formed the living soul of the faithful through affections set in order by the vigor of continence; and after that You renewed after Your image and likeness the mind that is subject to You alone and needs to imitate no human authority; and You made its rational action subject to the excellence of the understanding, as the woman to the man. And You willed that, for all the Offices of Your Ministry needed for perfecting the faithful in this life, good things for their temporal uses should be given by those same faithful, things that will bear fruit for themselves in time to come. All these we see, and they are very good, because You see them in us, You who have given us Your Spirit, by which we might see them and in them love You.

O Lord God, give us peace (for You have given us all things): the peace of rest, the peace of the Sabbath, which has no evening. For all this most beautiful array of things that are very good will pass away once their courses are complete; for in them there was morning and evening.

But the seventh day has no evening and no setting, because You have sanctified it to last for ever; so that the voice of Your Book may announce to us beforehand, through what You did when You rested on the seventh day after Your works which were very good — although You made them while remaining at rest — that we too, after our works (which are very good because You have given them to us), shall rest in You in the Sabbath of eternal life.

For then You will rest in us, just as now You work in us; and so that rest will be Yours through us, just as these works are Yours through us. But You, Lord, are always working and always at rest. You do not see in time, nor are You moved in time, nor do You rest in time; and yet You make the things that are seen in time, and the times themselves, and the rest which results from time.

So we see these things that You made because they are; but they are because You see them. And we see outwardly that they are, and inwardly that they are good; but You saw them made there where You saw them yet to be made. And at a later time we were moved to do good, after our heart had conceived from Your Spirit; but in the former time we were moved to do evil, forsaking You. But You, the One, the Good God, have never ceased to do good. And we also have some good works, by Your gift, but they are not eternal; after them we hope to rest in Your great hallowing. But You, being the Good that needs no good, are always at rest, because Your rest is You Yourself. And what man can teach another man to understand this? Or what Angel can teach an Angel? Or what Angel a man? Let it be asked of You, sought in You, knocked for at Your door; so, so shall it be received, so shall it be found, so shall it be opened. Amen.
GRATIAS TIBI DOMINE
